title: Quota fallthrough & per-route debugging notes (wireframes + backlog)
body:
PURPOSE

Quick working notes for a focused feature set: help engineers and SREs understand why requests were throttled/failed at the credential or route level, visualize fallback/fallthrough behavior, and provide a step-through debugging surface that ties telemetry to the exact decision that changed runtime behavior. This is intentionally product-facing (console) but designed to be actionable for on-call and devs.

PROBLEM STATEMENT

Observations from support and SRE: when customers hit degraded performance or unexpected rejections they often can't tell: was it a quota, a route-level throttle, a global throttling event, or a model fallback? Current per-key and per-route pages are fragmented: token charts, top routes, and raw logs exist but no single surface shows decision lineage (which policy -> which limit -> when did fallback trigger).

PRIMARY USER PERSONAS

- Platform engineer (oncall): needs a fast signal + root cause to remediate (e.g., increase capacity, change routing policy).
- Product engineer (implements SDKs): needs to see request examples and local reproduce steps.
- Solutions engineer / CSM: needs to explain behavior to customers and propose short/medium-term mitigations.

OVERVIEW OF PROPOSED SURFACES (wireframe text)

1) "Fallthrough Map" (console landing card)
   - Compact heatmap showing per-credential x per-route grid for the selected time window (default last 3 hours). Color legend: green=OK, yellow=soft-throttle (delayed), orange=rate-limit-reached (queued/dropped), red=rejects.
   - Hover state: show small pop-up with counts (tokens, requests, throttled_count, rejects) and top 2 policies that applied.
   - Row header: credential id alias and team tag. Column header: high-level route group (chat.generate, embeddings.create, rerank).
   - Click a cell -> opens "Inspector flyout" for that credential+route.

2) Inspector flyout (right-hand panel)
   - Top: summary line: "12.6k tokens, 4.2k reqs, 18% throttled, fallback to model-x at 2025-03-02T10:42Z".
   - Timeline sparkline with markers for policy state transitions: normal -> burst-protection -> fallback. Markers are interactive.
   - Sample request list (paginated) with request id, timestamp, token count, result status (200/429/503), applied_policy_id, latency p50/p95. Clicking a request shows full request+response headers and example payload (with PII redaction).
   - "Why this request was throttled" diagnostic: a short, autogenerated sentence combining rules (e.g., "Throttled because per-route QPS limit 150 was exceeded for credential ABC at 10:41:22. Global fallback policy then routed to smaller model.")
   - Quick actions: increase temporary cap (1-click propose a bump), add key to whitelist for 10m, open a support/incident link prefilled with context.

3) Route-level timeline page (full page)
   - Long chart area with stacked lines: requests, throttled, rejected, fallback activations. Secondary axis: token spend. Annotations layer for incidents / deploys.
   - Ability to toggle aggregation: by credential, by region, by model.
   - Query bar to search for specific policy ids, route tags, or credential alias. Export CSV for selected time window.

4) Replay / reproduce helper (experimental)
   - For requests kept in the request cache: ability to replay request against a mirror environment (read-only) to see whether it would be throttled now (useful for config/regression testing). Requires infra feature gate and audit log.

MICRO-INTERACTIONS & COPY NOTES

- When a cell in Fallthrough Map is clicked the flyout slides open; the cell remains highlighted with a thin blue ring.
- For the autogenerated "why" sentence avoid jargon: prefer "per-route request rate" over "QPS" in flyout copy; use QPS in advanced telemetry details.
- Tooltips should be terse and show exact counts + time of peak.
- Errors states: show "No data" with suggestions: widen time window, check credential alias, check that ingestion for the region is enabled.

TELEMETRY & EVENTS (what product needs from infra)

List of events we want surfaced for the inspector to build the sentence & timeline:
- request.received (id, timestamp, route, credential, tokens, region)
- policy.check (request_id, policy_id, decision {allow,delay,throttle,reject}, reason_code)
- throttle.enqueued (queue_depth, timeout_ms)
- throttle.rejected (backoff_seconds, reason)
- fallback.activated (from_model, to_model, timestamp, triggered_by) 
- quota.snapshot (credential, route, window_start, window_end, consumed_tokens, limit_tokens)

Each event should be queryable by request id and time range. Need a low-cardinality join key (request_id) passed through all hops. (Note: we discussed costs of storing raw logs — discuss retention policy separately.)

BACKLOG (groomed, with rough sizing & priority)

P0 - MVP (sprint 1, 2 engineers, 4w)
- Fallthrough Map (frontend) - interactive grid, hover popups, click opens flyout. (3pts)
- Inspector flyout core (summary, timeline sparkline, why sentence using policy.check events) (5pts)
- Basic request list (id, ts, tokens, status) with link-to-raw-logs (3pts)
- Telemetry contract doc + small infra shim to attach policy.check to request logs (backend) (3pts)

P1 - near-term (sprint 2-3)
- Route-level timeline page with toggles/aggregation (5pts)
- Quick actions (propose bump, temporary whitelist) — UI + backend api + audit log (5pts)
- Export CSV and permalink share (2pts)

P2 - experimental/opt-in (quarterly)
- Replay helper (gated) + sandbox execution environment (8pts)
- Autodetect correlated spikes across credentials and surface group-level suggestions (8pts)
- Compact mobile-friendly fallthrough card for Slack/Teams alerts (3pts)

Open design/ops questions (not groomed yet)

- Retention for request-level logs required for meaningful "why" prose. Minimum recommended: 7 days; ideal 30 days. Confirm with infra on cost impact.
- How do we sign and show PII-redacted payloads safely? KMS requirement? We'll need policy for scrub and a demo implementation on dev cluster.
- How will RBAC interact with quick actions (only owners/admins can bump)? Need mapping to org/team model in identity service.

ACCESSIBILITY & PERFORMANCE CONSIDERATIONS

- Fallthrough Map can be large for orgs with many keys and many routes. Default collapse to top-25 by traffic; provide an "expand" lazy-load option.
- Use canvas rendering for heatmap if cell count > 2k to keep 60fps on modern browsers.
- Ensure all interactive elements have keyboard focus states and ARIA labels.

EXAMPLE UX COPY (for designers/devs to drop in)

- Summary header: "Credential: ember-service-01 · Route: chat.generate · Last 3 hours"
- Why sentence: "Requests were throttled when the route-level burst limit (150 QPS) was exceeded between 10:41 and 10:47; 42 requests were queued and 7 rejected. A fallback to model-micro was triggered at 10:42:11."
- Empty state suggestions: "No recorded throttles in this window. Try increasing window to 24h or select a different route."

NEXT STEPS (owner: Ava)

- Sync with infra (Diego) to confirm feasibility of request-level event joins and retention tradeoffs (due 2025-02-17).
- Quick sketch of fallthrough map tile sizes and grid behaviour (Priya) - due 2025-02-14.
- Create a minimal backend shim PR that attaches policy.check to request logs (Samir). Link: GH-PR-9874.
- Review RBAC mapping with Identity (sprint 3 planning).

NOTES / TO SELF

- Keep the initial "why" sentence short and actionable — avoid dumping raw policy ids unless user clicks "advanced details".
- This surface should be read-only by default; quick actions are opt-in per org to avoid accidental bumping.
- Consider a separate smaller view for customer-facing CSMs that strips internal policy ids and shows only human-friendly explanations.

END OF NOTES
